title: Identification of Parent User via Registration Data
description: The registration flow collects multiple personally identifiable information (email, name, government ID) that can be used to uniquely identify the parent user. This identification occurs at the source of the data flow.
assumptions: The system stores and processes this PII without adequate anonymization or pseudonymization.

title: Linkability of Registration Data Across Systems
description: The collected registration data (email, name, government ID) can be linked across different systems or databases, potentially enabling correlation of the parent user's activities and identity across multiple contexts.
assumptions: The data may be shared with third parties or stored in multiple systems without proper linkage controls.

title: Disclosure of Sensitive Registration Data
description: The authentication service may disclose sensitive registration data (password, government ID, email) to unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, data breaches, or improper transmission security.
assumptions: The authentication service lacks proper encryption, access controls, or data protection measures for the sensitive information being processed.

title: Usurpation of Parent User Identity
description: The combination of email, password, name, and government ID collected during registration could be exploited for identity theft or account takeover, allowing unauthorized parties to impersonate the parent user.
assumptions: The authentication service may not implement adequate authentication mechanisms, password hashing, or multi-factor authentication to prevent identity usurpation.

title: Non-compliance with Data Protection Regulations
description: The collection and processing of government ID and other sensitive personal data during parent registration may violate data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) if proper consent, data minimization, and retention policies are not implemented.
assumptions: The authentication service may not have adequate legal basis, consent mechanisms, or data governance policies for processing sensitive personal data.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of parent account data
description: The authentication service may disclose parent account information to unauthorized parties through improper access controls, network vulnerabilities, or misconfigured data sharing mechanisms.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls or security misconfigurations exist in the authentication service or its communication channels.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 as a general data disclosure node; specific node may vary based on exact disclosure mechanism.

title: Data store exposure of parent account information
description: The MongoDB users collection may expose parent account data to unauthorized access through insufficient encryption, weak authentication, or improper access controls on the data store.
assumptions: MongoDB instance lacks proper security hardening or access controls.
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 is a general disclosure node; specific MongoDB security context not fully captured.

title: Identification of individuals through parent account data
description: Parent account information stored in the authentication service can be used to identify specific individuals, potentially enabling profiling or targeted attacks.
assumptions: Parent account data contains sufficient personally identifiable information to uniquely identify individuals.
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 is a general identification node; specific identification vectors depend on data content.

title: Tampering with parent account records
description: The MongoDB users collection may be subject to unauthorized modification, leading to corrupted or falsified parent account information.
assumptions: Inadequate integrity controls or authentication mechanisms exist for the data store.
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 is a general data integrity node; specific tampering vectors depend on access controls.

title: Usurpation of parent account identity
description: An attacker may exploit the authentication service to impersonate legitimate users by gaining unauthorized access to parent account credentials or session data.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms have vulnerabilities or session management is inadequate.
uncertainty_note: U.1.1 is a general usurpation node; specific authentication vulnerabilities not fully characterized.

title: User Identifiability via JWT Token
description: The JWT token transmitted from the Authentication Service to the Parent User contains user data that can directly identify the individual. This creates a privacy risk as the Parent User (external entity) receives personally identifiable information.
assumptions: JWT contains user-identifying information and Parent User has access to this data

title: Linkability of User Data Across Systems
description: The JWT and user data sent to the Parent User can be linked to other data sources or systems, potentially creating a comprehensive profile of the user across multiple contexts.
assumptions: Parent User may correlate this data with other information sources

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of User Data
description: The transmission of JWT and user data to the Parent User (external entity) creates a risk of unauthorized disclosure if the Parent User is not properly authorized or if the data is intercepted during transmission.
assumptions: Parent User may not have proper authorization or data may be intercepted

title: User Identity Usurpation via JWT Token
description: The JWT token could be stolen or misused by unauthorized parties to impersonate the user, as JWT tokens can be intercepted and potentially replayed without proper cryptographic verification.
assumptions: JWT may not have adequate cryptographic protection or may be transmitted insecurely

title: Data Integrity Compromise of JWT Token
description: The JWT token and user data could be altered or tampered with during transmission to the Parent User, leading to data integrity issues and potential unauthorized modifications to user information.
assumptions: Transmission channel may not be fully secured or JWT may lack proper signature verification

title: Child login activity linked to parent identity
description: Child user's login activity using parent email credentials can be linked to the parent's identity, potentially exposing the child's online behavior to the parent or third parties who can access parent account information.
assumptions: Parent email is used as authentication credential and parent account information is accessible
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 chosen based on context mapping for ExternalEntity->Process flows

title: Child identity usurpation through parent credentials
description: Child user may be able to impersonate or usurp parent identity by using parent email/password, or parent credentials may be misused by unauthorized parties, creating identity confusion and access control issues.
assumptions: Parent credentials are shared with child and authentication service accepts parent credentials for child login
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 chosen based on context mapping for ExternalEntity->Process flows

title: Child login credentials disclosed to unauthorized parties
